# opv

> opv is a Rust CLI that syncs secrets from 1Password into runtime targets (Fly.io, Azure Key Vault + Container Apps, Kubernetes, and Key Vault → Kubernetes through the External Secrets Operator supported; Azure App Service, AWS and GCP planned) and into local processes (`opv run`) without ever printing, logging or writing a secret value. A project manifest in 1Password (Secure Note `opv · <project>`, found by the git remote) or a committed `secrets.toml` with the same TOML declares IDs, key names, kinds and validation rules; values stay in 1Password.

## Contract (read this first)

- Start with `opv schema`: one JSON document describing the installed binary (commands, flags, what each changes and whether to ask first, exit codes, the stable error codes, JSON shapes).
- Safe without asking (change nothing): `opv schema`, `opv doctor`, `opv status` (and `status --all`), `opv plan`, `opv check`, `opv explain`, `opv open --print`, `opv projects`, `opv help states`, `opv guide agent`, `opv config export` (prints config values only, never secrets), `opv config check`, `opv completions`, `--help`, `--version`. Run by the user's own signed-in session (`opv login`), any command that reads an item may tidy its layout once (nothing deleted; listed in `tidy`); service accounts, CI and deploy credentials never write. `opv add` and `opv init --add-env` on a `secrets.toml` only edit the repository.
- Ask the user first, every time: `opv item skeleton` (writes empty fields to an item), `opv config import`, `opv init` in a new project and `opv add` on a configuration in 1Password (they write the project's manifest, names only), `opv sync`, and the flags `--deploy`, `--prune`, `--rotate`, `--prune-immutable`, `--confirm`. Apply a reviewed plan with `opv sync <env> --expect-plan <id>` (the id `opv plan` printed); it refuses if anything changed.
- Hand to the user, never run yourself: `opv setup`, `opv login <env>` and `opv config edit` (they need the user's own terminal).
- Never read or ask for a value: no `op read`, `op item get --reveal`, `op inject`, `op run -- env`.
- Every failure ends with one `Next: <command>` line, the last line on stderr: a command that runs as-is. Run it (or show it); do not invent workarounds. A `Do:` line, when present, is a human action for the user (for example filling a field in 1Password). A configuration error names `file:line: field` and its `Do:` line is the edit.
- Prefer `--json` (every command whose `opv schema` entry has `"json": true`; `run`, `login`, `setup`, `config edit`, `config import` and `config check` do not take it): stdout is one document on success and on failure, `{schema_version, ok, ..., next, do}` plus `error: {code, category, message, detail, retry, human_required, do, next}` on failure. Branch on `error.code`, never the message: e.g. `unknown_env`, `config_not_found`, `manifest_not_found`, `keys_blocking`, `confirm_required`, `stale_plan`, `terminal_required`, `op_not_signed_in`, `deploy_credentials_failed`, `ram_dir_unavailable`, `findings`, `outcome_unknown` (`opv schema` lists all). Re-run only when `retry` is `safe`, or `after_fix` once `do` is done; when `human_required` is true hand `do` and `next` to the user.
- Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 config or usage (fix first); 3 a CLI is missing (install it); 4 1Password; 5 target; 6 refused (`error.code` says which: `keys_blocking`, `confirm_required`, `stale_plan`, `terminal_required`, `ram_dir_unavailable`, `policy_refused`); 7 not signed in; 8 findings from status, plan or check; 9 outcome unknown, safe to re-run as is (CI may retry); 130/143 interrupted, safe to re-run. Codes 2 to 8 need a fix before a retry.
- `opv guide agent` prints the agent setup guide for the installed version. Prefer it to the web copies below, which follow `main`.

Assistants setting opv up for a user: read the agent setup guide first and follow its rules. Never ask the user for a secret value, never read one (`op item get --reveal`, `op read`), and ask before `opv item skeleton`, `opv sync`, `--deploy`, `--prune`, `--rotate`, `--prune-immutable` or `--confirm`. On Azure and Kubernetes `sync` writes new secret versions and the app changes only with `--deploy`. Exit 9 means the outcome is unknown or a provider did not answer: nothing is known to be broken, re-run the same command. Declare keys with `opv add`, environments with `opv init --add-env`, and keep the configuration in 1Password with `opv config import` (projects: `opv projects`). `opv run` always passes `op://` references, so `op run` masks values in the child's output. `Next:` / `next` is always one runnable command; `Do:` / `do` is the user's part.

## Docs

- [Agent setup guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/agent-setup.md): step-by-step setup for AI assistants, with safety rules and exit codes
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/README.md): what opv is, quickstart, minimal configuration
- [Installing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/install.md): install script, binaries, npm, source, checksum verification, prerequisites
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/configuration.md): where the configuration lives (manifest discovery, monorepo paths, `config import/export/edit/check`), the schema, simple and fleet profiles, store layout, Fly, Azure and Kubernetes targets, named stores (`[stores.<name>]` + `secrets_in`: Key Vault → Kubernetes via the External Secrets Operator), shared keys, `opv init` and `opv add`, rules and failure reasons
- [Local development](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/local-development.md): `opv run`, `opv check`, run-only environments, several products, WSL
- [Guided setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/guided-setup.md): `opv login` and `opv setup` (the user's own terminal)
- [Usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/usage.md): every command and flag, sync on Fly, Azure and Kubernetes, the JSON contract and error codes, exit codes, security model, GitHub Actions
- [How opv handles failures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matt-cochran/1password-vault/main/docs/how-opv-handles-failures.md): `Next:`/`Do:`, retries, time limits, exit 9, interruptions, scrubbed CLI output
